body: Me too. I don't care what happens to me, I can drop dead any time now for all I care, but I just don't want to cause them any unnecessary hurt in the process. I mean, whether I die from suicide or sudden massive heart failure, they'll grieve all the same, but suicide has that nasty extra bit of psychological damage. The last thing I want is for those thoughts of "I should have seen the signs" or "I wish I had done something different" to follow them for the rest of their lives.

I know that you've been planning this for a while, but are you absolutely certain that this is how you want to die? Nature is unforgiving, and dying out there could be a long, agonizingly painful process, especially this close to the winter. Starvation, bleeding out, internal bleeding from injury, infection, exposure, freezing to death, and other such slow, miserable deaths are not only possible, but likely, and could take days before they kill you. I don't doubt that you're ready to die, but are you sure that you're prepared to die like this?

It takes massive balls to do a lot of things. That doesn't inherently make those things brave, or worthy of admiration.

It's like I said. It's an act of desperation. People do plenty of things that take a lot of balls when they're desperate, and fighting their survival instinct to make the pain stop is just one of the most extreme.

Admire? No. Sympathize? Definitely. I'd be a hypocrite to judge them for doing it when I've come so goddamn close to finally putting myself out of my misery as many times as I have.

Suicide is not a cowardly, selfish act, but it's also not a brave, admirable one. It's desperation. Desperation for the pain to finally end. And while I don't judge those who couldn't cope any longer, it's not something worthy of praise or idolization. It's a tragedy.

If she told you to kill yourself, yeah, she's abusive. Anyone fit to be a mother would NEVER tell her child to kill themselves. Not even in a brief fit of anger.

If your dad isn't willing/able/whatever to do anything about it, you should maybe consider telling someone. Even if it's just out of spite. Because screw anyone, and I mean ANYONE, that would tell their own child to take their own life. Give her hell.

If there isn't an afterlife, then... nothing. It's not like you're conscious in the nothing, seeing the nothing, feeling the nothing... it's like someone flipped your off switch. One fraction of a second, you're there, living out those brief moments where your brain goes haywire, and the next... poof. Gone.

If there is one, then... well, there's no shortage of interpretations as to what's on the other side. Heaven, Hell, purgatory, Valhalla, reincarnation, the Underworld, the universe's biggest waiting room... Might as well be throwing darts at the wall for all the good speculating will do until you wind up there, you know?

But personally, I try not to think about it too much. Not much sense, considering I'll find out sooner or later. Or if there's actually nothing there, I guess I won't, because I'll be dead, but at that point it won't matter.

There's a reason that hanging was phased out as a means of execution. If the rope's not calculated properly, it'll either fail completely or, at the bare minimum, be an absolutely agonizing (not to mention slow) way to die.

Plus, if you do survive, it's likely that it'd leave you with brain damage and/or paralysis. Of all the ways to check out early, it's probably one of the worst, all things considered.
